questions.text: Charging two uncharged objects by rubbing them together is called charging by ______.
The accumulation of electric charges on object surfaces is called ______ electricity.
The region around an electric charge in which its effect appears is called the electric ______.
Charging an uncharged object by touching it with another charged object is charging by ______.
In the electrostatic series, when two materials are rubbed, the material higher in the series tends to become:
Compare electrically conducting and nonconducting materials.
questions.answer: Conductors allow electric charges to flow through them; insulators do not allow charges to flow easily.

questions.text: Give a reason: A copper rod should have an insulating wooden handle when rubbed.
questions.answer: Because copper conducts electric charge, while wood is an electrical insulator.

questions.text: Give a reason: A person may feel a slight electric shock after walking barefoot on a carpet and touching a metal handle.
questions.answer: Static charge formed by friction discharges through the metal handle.

questions.text: Give a reason: Fuel transport vehicles use metal chains touching the ground.
questions.answer: To discharge static electricity produced by friction and reduce ignition risk.

questions.text: Give a reason: Two silk pieces rubbed separately with cotton repel each other.
questions.answer: Both acquire the same type of electric charge, and like charges repel.

questions.text: A device used to detect whether an object is electrically charged is the ______.
Give a reason: The leaves of an electroscope diverge after a charged object touches its disc.
questions.answer: The leaves acquire like charges and repel each other.

questions.text: Compare charging by friction and charging by contact.
questions.answer: Friction charges two initially uncharged materials by electron transfer during rubbing; contact charges an uncharged object by touching it with a charged object.

questions.text: Give a reason: Electric field lines do not intersect.
questions.answer: At any point the electric field has one definite direction, so two field lines cannot cross.

questions.answer: To discharge any residual electric charge and return the electroscope to a neutral state.

questions.text: Consultant-generated application: A charged object brought near an electroscope changes leaf divergence without touching. What does this demonstrate?
questions.answer: Electric force can act at a distance through an electric field.
